At $12.99, it's the smartest outlet upgrade you can buy. --- ## The Case for a Good Surge Protector Power strips are ugly. Extension cords are tripping hazards. The solution is a wall-mounted outlet extender that replaces the strip entirely — and that's where these two products compete. A quality surge protector isn't just about quantity of outlets — it's about: - **Joule rating** (how much surge energy it can absorb) - **Port selection** (USB-C is standard now, not a luxury) - **Form factor** (does it block the second outlet?) - **Extra features** (night lights, rotating plugs, smart compatibility) --- ## Addtam Surge Protector Outlet Extender — The Complete Package The [**Addtam Surge Protector Outlet Extender**](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09XMMZSWW?tag=worthitgoods-20) has quietly become one of the most popular wall outlet extenders on Amazon, and for good reason — it solves almost every complaint people have about power strips. ### Key Specs - **AC Outlets:** 5 (3 front + 2 side) - **USB Ports:** 3 total (2 USB-A + 1 USB-C 3.0A) - **Surge Protection:** 800 Joules - **Night Light:** LED, soft warm glow - **Plug Design:** 45° rotating, low-profile - **Weight:** 5.6 oz - **Coverage:** Fits behind furniture up against wall ### What Makes It Great **The USB-C port is the headline feature.** While Belkin still uses two USB-A ports (ancient by 2026 standards), Addtam includes a proper USB-C fast-charge port that handles phones, tablets, and even the latest laptops at full speed. No more hunting for a charging brick. **Rotating 45° plug** means it doesn't block the second outlet on your duplex. This is huge — most competitors force you to sacrifice an entire outlet. Addtam leaves the lower outlet fully usable. **The built-in night light** is surprisingly useful. It's a soft LED that's bright enough to find in the dark but dim enough not to disturb sleep. The light can be toggled on/off independently. ### Potential Drawbacks - 800 Joules is adequate but not the highest available - USB-C port is 3.0A (15W) — not the 65W+ you'd want for a MacBook Pro - No individual outlet switches --- ## Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector — The Legacy Name [**Belkin**](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08GHXK2B3?tag=worthitgoods-20) has been making surge protectors since the 1990s, and their reputation for quality is well-earned. But in the wall-mounted outlet extender space, they're playing catch-up. ### Key Specs - **AC Outlets:** 6 - **USB Ports:** 2 (both USB-A, shared 2.4A) - **Surge Protection:** Up to 1000 Joules (depends on model) - **Form Factor:** Traditional power strip with cord - **Plug Design:** Fixed, right-angle - **Cord Length:** 3-6 ft (depends on model) ### What Makes It Good Belkin's build quality is excellent. The casing feels dense, the outlets grip plugs firmly, and the company backs their products with a connected equipment warranty ($200k-$300k depending on model). That's peace of mind. The **6 outlets** are all spaced widely enough to fit bulky transformer plugs (a pet peeve of power strip users). ### Where It Falls Short - **No USB-C.** In 2026, this is hard to justify at $29.99. - **Traditional corded power strip** — not a wall extender. It takes up space on your desk or floor. - **No night light** — a feature that costs pennies to add. - **$29.99 for fewer features than Addtam's $12.99** — the value gap is striking. --- ## Head-to-Head Comparison ### USB Ports Addtam has USB-C fast charging. Belkin has two USB-A ports. USB-A is effectively obsolete for fast charging. **Edge: Addtam (by a wide margin)** ### Form Factor Addtam mounts flush to the wall with a rotating plug that doesn't block the second outlet. Belkin's corded design means clutter, tripping hazards, and lost desk space. **Edge: Addtam** ### Surge Protection Belkin's 1000 Joule rating is technically higher than Addtam's 800. For most household electronics, 800 Joules is sufficient — it'll handle a typical lightning surge or power fluctuation. If you're protecting a home theater or server rack, spend more on a whole-home protector. **Edge: Belkin (by a small margin, for heavy gear)** ### Extra Features Addtam's night light is a genuinely useful addition that Belkin doesn't match. **Edge: Addtam** ### Price $12.99 vs $29.99.
